newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says withdrawing Cambodia trade office.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says withdrawing Cambodia trade office.

text.p: Taiwan said on Monday it was withdrawing its unofficial trade office in Phnom Penh, which Cambodian strongman Hun Sen had ordered shut after alleging Taiwanese interference in his country's political turmoil.
Taipei also ordered Phnom Penh to close its unofficial office in the Taiwan capital.

"In consideration of our dignity and interests, we have decided to shut the representative office and withdraw our representatives there," foreign ministry spokesman Roy Wu told reporters. Office chief Chu Che-chuan returned home on Sunday.

Wu said closing Taiwan's office would affect Taiwanese investment in Cambodia, but stopped short of urging a boycott by Taiwan investors, who collectively rank as the top source of investment in Cambodia's unsteady, war-scarred economy.
"We urge caution for our citizens going there for tourism or investment," Wu said.

Wu blamed the row on Taiwan's arch rival, communist China, suggesting Beijing was calling the shots in Phnom Penh and now was extending its longtime diplomatic embargo of what it regards as a renegade province to other non-official spheres.

"Very clearly the Chinese communists are the black hand behind (Cambodia's) barbaric and irrational behaviour," Wu said. "The reason is simple. The Chinese communists want to clamp down on all our activities in all realms, whether official or unofficial."
Cambodia recognises only Beijing and has no official ties with Taipei.
